text:
Asha: FYI found a scope enforcement bug affecting API keys scoped to embeddings. Keys with only `embeddings:read` can hit the chat endpoint and return generations. Repro below.

Asha: repro (minimal):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test-REDACTED" \n  -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
# returns 200 and a completion
```

Asha: relevant log (filtered):
```
auth: allowed key=sk-test-REDACTED scopes=["embeddings:read"] route=/v1/chat/completions status=200 session_id=abc123
```

Ben: whoa. Thanks for flagging. Do you have the key id and when it was created?

Asha: key id sk-ky_42, created 2025-11-02T14:12Z. Only used by analytics embedding pipeline.

Carlos: this smells like the RBAC refactor from PR #432 — we changed how route->scope mapping is computed and added a fallback that can treat `/v1/*` routes as matching multiple resource patterns. If scope check is doing prefix substring instead of exact resource match, embeddings-only scopes could match `model:*/embeddings` and `model:*/chat` incorrectly.

Rachel: immediate mitigations: 1) rotate/revoke affected keys, 2) enable strict scope enforcement flag `auth.strict_scope=true` on prod for a canary region, 3) add audit log marker for all token-scope mismatches. I'll start key revocations. @Carlos can you prep a quick hotfix? :warning:

deploy-bot: rollback deployed: reverted commit 9f4b2a (rbac-enforcement) — rollback started 2026-03-10T17:11Z, finished 2026-03-10T17:14Z :white_check_mark:

audit-bot: recorded event id=e-20260310-7788 type=auth_scope_violation candidate_key=sk-ky_42 actor=Asha

Ben: question: does rotating our KMS CMK for dedicated customers invalidate existing encrypted API keys/tokens? Need to know impact if we recommend mass rotation.

Carlos: short answer: rotating KMS key material (automatic yearly rotation) doesn't change DEKs kept in DB; we rewrap with new CMK but that happens on-the-fly. However, if a customer uses an external KMS where we can't rewrap automatically, tokens that require local unwrap could fail until rewrapped. For our hosted keys, rotation is safe. For Private/Dedicated with customer-managed KMS, ops needs to coordinate rewrap.

Asha: OK. For now I've revoked the single affected key and added a temporary guard in front of auth that rejects any request where requested operation != scopes intersection. Patch link: https://git.internal/r/priv/patches/1287

Carlos: proposed permanent fix (will open PR): enforce exact resource->scope mapping in auth middleware, update matcher to use token.scopes set vs route.required_scope and avoid prefix matching. Add unit tests: embeddings-only key cannot call chat and vice-versa. Example policy JSON for matcher:
```json
{
  "required_scope": "embeddings:read",
  "resource": "models/gpt-*/embeddings"
}
```

Rachel: also add an audit rule to emit `scope_mismatch` for any allow that required a fallback. We need traceability for compliance audits.

Ben: agree. Also add a migration to verify all existing keys have explicit scope arrays (no legacy empty scopes).

Asha: I'll open an incident ticket with timeline, keys revoked, and next steps. Owner: Asha (visibility: security + infra + compliance).

Carlos: will send a hotfix PR for the middleware and tests, target hotfix branch and a canary rollout. If tests pass, we can re-enable the stricter enforcement flag and monitor audit stream.

Rachel: follow-up checklist for tasks: revoke affected keys, hotfix PR #TBD, runbook update (inc/008-auth-scope-rotation), audit event retention extended for 90 days, customer outreach template.

Asha: thanks all. I'll post incident summary when ticket is created. :memo:
